review_notes:
I read the whole file and the simp-related declarations in Mathlib/Algebra/Group/PUnit.lean (`one_eq`, `div_eq`, `inv_eq` are simp; `mul_eq` is deliberately not simp, with a comment explaining why). I also searched Mathlib for uses of `PUnit.commRing`, `Nat.cast` into `PUnit`, and other PUnit ring lemmas. The file has no simp lemmas or attributes of its own. Its only simp use is `by simp` in the `IsCancelMulZero` instance. That use depends on the `Subsingleton` simp set, and the `PUnit.commRing` use sites I found (BooleanRing.lean, Normed/Ring/Basic.lean, FiveLemma.lean) don't depend on any ring-level simp lemma.

A lemma saying `(n : PUnit) = unit` could in principle be added for `natCast _ := unit`. I found no downstream use that needs it, so recommending it would be adding a simp annotation only because the identity looks simple. I found no competing rules, bad orientations or rewrite cycles. The small uncertainty is that I did not run Lean, so I did not check that `simp` closes `Nat.cast` goals on `PUnit` through `Subsingleton`.
